## UX review: skill pages a11y-audit, copy-tight, spec-writer Reviewed: Header and first section of three skill pages built from one template (code only). Layout input: none. Main goal: install the skill shown on the page Steps to main goal: 1 (Install section, Copy install command) Findings: 2 (S1: 0, S2: 1, S3: 1, S4: 0) ### Findings 1. **Header on the skill-page template, on 3 pages: skills/a11y-audit.html, skills/copy-tight.html, skills/spec-writer.html** | S2 Major | R-ux-review-11 - Evidence: "Install" - User experiences: The user looking to install this skill clicks the header Install link, lands on the collection page, and has to find the way back to the skill. - Recommendation: Make the header link that leaves the skill page carry a label different from the page's own Install section, or take the user to this skill's install section. 2. **spec-writer page, Compare section** | S3 Minor | R-ux-review-30 - Evidence: "

Compare

" - User experiences: The user sees two equal primary install buttons in one view and stops to work out whether they differ. - Recommendation: Keep one primary install action in the view and make any second install control visibly secondary, or remove it from the Compare section. ### Not reviewed - Contrast, focus styles, spacing and type scales: a visual polish pass. - Semantics, ARIA and screen-reader output: an accessibility audit. - Wording of labels and messages: a copy edit. ### Open questions - Copy install command button (all pages): the input shows no handler, so whether the click gives a visible "copied" confirmation is not shown. - Install section (all pages): the install command itself is not shown, so whether the user can see what was copied is not shown. - Header links and Copy install command button: no styles or sizes are given, so how they look and whether each target is at least 44 by 44 px with 8 px gaps is not shown. - Pages (all): only the header and first section are given. Page height, first-screen order and the count of clickable controls on the first screen are not shown. ### Severity scale - S1 Blocker: the user cannot complete the main goal, or loses data or money. - S2 Major: the user completes the main goal only after a wrong action, an error or a second attempt. - S3 Minor: the user completes the main goal at the first attempt, but more slowly. - S4 Note: the result and the speed do not change; the place departs from the rule.
